gaps.explanation: Statement p7 (Utilities, cash basis) total receipts 1,824,087 = user fees 1,552,188 + late charges 29,061 + interest 2,285 + grants and contributions 233,978 + miscellaneous 6,575. The only schedule, p11 (Utilities, accrual basis), prints operating revenues 1,592,741 (user fees 1,557,105, late charges 29,061, miscellaneous 6,575) + interest income 2,285 = 1,595,026 and has no grants line. The accrual cash flow schedule p12 explains the whole difference: 'Increase in deferred revenue' 233,978 (the cash grants are deferred, not accrual revenue) and 'Increase in receivables' (4,917) (user fees 1,557,105 accrued vs 1,552,188 collected). 1,824,087 - 1,595,026 = 229,061 = 233,978 - 4,917, exact. No line is missing from the p11 schedule; no fix.

Statement p7 (cash basis) total disbursements 1,927,752 = general administrative 391,760 + production and distribution 1,103,865 + debt service principal 390,000 + interest 42,127. Schedule p11 (accrual basis) total operating expenses 1,196,612 + interest and fiscal fees 39,708 = 1,236,320, including depreciation and amortization 632,100 and excluding capital purchases and bond principal. Per the cash flow schedule p12: 1,236,320 - depreciation 632,100 + purchase of capital assets 774,940 + principal payment on bonds 390,000 + interest paid 42,127 vs 39,708 (+2,419) + decrease in payables and accrued expenses 156,179 = 1,927,758, within 6 of the cash statement 1,927,752 (the p12 cash flows themselves differ from the p7 cash statement by small amounts: p12 net decrease in cash 103,904 vs p7 103,665, incl. CD purchase 233). Gap 691,432 is the accrual vs cash basis difference; no detail line is missing; no fix.
